messages:
Maria: Heads-up — I'm revising the provisioning playbook for saturn-south-1 (new region bring-up). Main things to add: GPU quota edge cases, NIC/MTU validation, known kernel-driver mismatches, and an explicit fallback routing section. Looking for quick reviewers + oncall sign-off. @Simon @Lee :eyes:
Simon: Ack. Can you list the quota failure modes you want in the doc? Cloud API sometimes returns 429 vs 403 and the message payload is inconsistent across regions.
Lee: We should include exact commands to check quotas + diff against expected capacity. I can paste the snippets. Also call out the soft-limit vs hard-limit behaviour we hit in west2 last year.
Maria: Good. Draft commands below — plz sanity-check and suggest edits:```bash
# check GPU quota for project
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://cloud.example.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT/quotas" | jq '.resources.gpu'
# quick node health probe
kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=gpu
# verify NIC MTU on hosts
ssh root@$HOST sudo ip link show dev eth0 | grep mtu
```
Tara: Add a small script to fail fast during bootstrap if GPUs reported = 0 or quota < requested. Also document the exact error strings we've observed (so oncall can search logs).
Maria: I'll add error-string examples. Simon, can you draft the fallback routing section? We want automated routing to a sibling region (saturn-north-1) when total capacity < threshold and cross-region latency < 50ms.
Simon: Yep. Proposed pseudo-policy: prefer same-region until utils/available_gpus < 10% then route to sibling region if cost delta < 2x. Include a manual override tag for customers needing strict locality.
Lee: Known issues to include (copied from recent incidents):
- NVidia driver mismatch: kernel >=5.15 + old nvidia-dkms can leave GPUs offline after node reboot. Workaround: `apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-dkms && reboot`
- MTU misconfig: some cloud images come with MTU 9000 but VPC is 1500 -> flows drop at 64KB. Fix: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500` and restart CNI.
- Quota race on creation: async quota updates show as available immediately but allocation later fails with 409. Add a 30s re-check loop after requesting quota.
Maria: Nice. For Troubleshooting guide section, propose this flow (short):
1) Validate quotas (curl + dashboard)
2) Confirm node provisioning logs (systemd + kubelet)
3) Check NV driver state (`nvidia-smi` / `dmesg | grep NVRM`)
4) Network tests (ping, iperf between nodes, MTU check)
5) If capacity short, escalate to capacity@ with region report + `available_gpus.json` attached.
Tara: Can you include the exact `kubectl` commands and the minimal JSON we want attached for capacity@? That makes triage faster.
Maria: Will add. Draft capacity report shape (example) and I'll include a sample snippet in the runbook. Also adding backoff timings for automated quota retries and a note about cost guardrails (don't auto-route to a region with >3x cost without human approval).
infra-bot: Reminder: runbook edits must pass docs linting (tools/runbook-lint) and include a YAML frontmatter with owners + last_reviewed date.
Lee: Quick question — should we include node-level kernel versions to pin in the image? We've had multiple incidents from auto-kernel bumps.
Simon: Yes, pin recommended kernels in the image build docs and add a 'compatible kernels' subsection to the runbook.
Maria: OK I'll produce a PR by EOD with all sections: quota checks, validation scripts, fallback routing policy, troubleshooting flow, known issues, and sample capacity report. Please review and leave comments in the PR rather than Slack. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Tara: Will review tomorrow morning.
Simon: I'll drop the routing pseudo-code into the PR as well.
Lee: Oncall sign-off: +1 once PR includes the 30s quota re-check and nvidia-driver rollback steps.
Maria: Got it — will include both. Closing loop here, PR incoming.
